subject: physiology
title: Hypothalamic Nuclei, Feeding Regulation, Leptin, and Ghrelin

steps.tx: Situated in the diencephalon beneath the thalamus and forming the floor of the third ventricle, the hypothalamus orchestrates whole-body physiological homeostasis. Critical **hypothalamic homeostatic functions** encompass neuroendocrine pituitary control, central autonomic regulation, body temperature maintenance, circadian timekeeping, thirst and water balance, feeding drive, and emotional expression.
steps.say: The hypothalamus integrates autonomic, endocrine, and behavioral systems to maintain body homeostasis.

vis.caption: Hypothalamic-pituitary neuroendocrine feedback loops regulating peripheral adrenocortical hormones.
vis.alt: Hypothalamic corticotropin-releasing hormone drive to pituitary corticotropes

steps.tx: Bilateral experimental stimulation or natural activation of the lateral hypothalamic area induces voracious, continuous food consumption. Acting as the physiological **feeding centre**, lateral hypothalamic neurons synthesize orexigenic neuropeptides including melanin-concentrating hormone and orexin, whereas bilateral lesions of this region result in severe aphagia and starvation.
steps.say: The lateral hypothalamic feeding centre promotes appetite, and its destruction leads to starvation.

left.title: Lateral Hypothalamus (Feeding Centre)
points: Promotes hyperphagia and feeding drive upon stimulation
Synthesizes orexin-A, orexin-B, and melanin-concentrating hormone
Bilateral ablation causes complete refusal to eat (aphagia) and cachexia
Receives inhibitory projections from satiety center following meal ingestion

right.title: Ventromedial Nucleus (Satiety Centre)
points: Terminates meal consumption upon gastrointestinal and nutrient signals
Expresses high concentrations of insulin and leptin receptors
Bilateral ablation causes relentless hyperphagia and morbid obesity
Exerts tonic inhibition over lateral hypothalamic feeding centers

steps.tx: Appetite has an off switch anatomically separate from its on switch. The **ventromedial satiety centre** signals fullness, and its bilateral destruction produces relentless eating and obesity in experimental animals, mirrored rarely by human hypothalamic tumours. Leptin from fat tissue is one of the voices this centre listens to. Damage here reframes severe obesity after pituitary surgery as neurology rather than willpower, changing how families are counselled.
steps.say: The ventromedial hypothalamus signals satiety and listens to leptin. Its damage causes relentless eating reframed as neurology, not willpower.

vis.alt: Image showing the ventromedial satiety centre of the hypothalamus.
vis.caption: The ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus is highlighted as the satiety centre. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In opposition to the lateral feeding center, the ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus functions as the physiological **satiety centre**. Stimulation of the ventromedial nucleus abruptly halts feeding, whereas bilateral destructive lesions eliminate postprandial satiety, producing unstoppable voracious hyperphagia, rapid gastric emptying, and intractable hypothalamic obesity.
steps.say: The ventromedial satiety centre stops eating, and its destruction causes voracious hyperphagia and obesity.

vis.caption: Severe neuroendocrine and metabolic dysregulation resulting from distorted central appetite circuits.
vis.alt: Profound metabolic and endocrine suppression in severe nutritional deprivation

steps.tx: Circulating long-term nutritional status is integrated within the arcuate nucleus by two competing neuronal populations. Pro-opiomelanocortin and cocaine-and-amphetamine-regulated transcript neurons synthesize alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone to activate melanocortin-4 receptors, promoting satiety, whereas **NPY and AgRP neurons** synthesize neuropeptide Y and agouti-related peptide to potently stimulate voracious eating.
steps.say: Arcuate POMC neurons promote satiety while NPY and AgRP neurons potently stimulate eating.

left.title: POMC / CART Neurons (Anorexigenic)
points: Stimulated by leptin, insulin, and postprandial gut hormones (GLP-1, PYY)
Cleaves POMC to release alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH)
Alpha-MSH binds melanocortin-4 receptors (MC4R) in paraventricular nucleus
Suppresses appetite and elevates basal metabolic energy expenditure

right.title: NPY / AgRP Neurons (Orexigenic)
points: Inhibited by leptin and insulin; stimulated by fasting and ghrelin
Releases neuropeptide Y (NPY) to stimulate Y1/Y5 hypothalamic receptors
Releases AgRP, an endogenous competitive antagonist at MC4 receptors
Drives relentless hunger, foraging behavior, and decreases metabolic rate

steps.tx: Secreted into the bloodstream by white adipose tissue in direct proportion to total body triglyceride stores, an essential protein hormone signals long-term energy sufficiency. This adipokine is **leptin**, which crosses the blood-brain barrier to stimulate anorexigenic POMC neurons while inhibiting orexigenic NPY/AgRP neurons within the arcuate nucleus.
steps.say: White adipose tissue secretes leptin in proportion to fat mass to signal satiety to the hypothalamus.

steps.tx: While leptin provides chronic adiposity feedback, meal initiation is triggered acutely by a peptide hormone synthesized primarily by oxyntic P/D1 endocrine cells of the gastric fundus. Designated **ghrelin**, this twenty-eight amino acid acylated peptide surges prior to expected meal times, stimulating arcuate NPY/AgRP neurons to provoke intense preprandial hunger.
steps.say: Gastric fundus cells secrete ghrelin before meals to stimulate NPY neurons and provoke acute hunger.

steps.tx: Following meal consumption, physical distension of the gastrointestinal tract and chemical nutrient absorption stimulate the rapid release of anorexigenic satiety peptides. Enteroendocrine L cells in the ileum and colon release **peptide YY and glucagon-like peptide 1**, which signal centrally via the vagus nerve and arcuate nucleus to terminate meal consumption.
steps.say: Intestinal L cells release GLP-1 and PYY after meals to terminate feeding and promote fullness.

left.title: Peptide YY (PYY3-36)
points: Secreted by mucosal L-cells of ileum and colon in response to fat and protein
Binds inhibitory presynaptic Y2 receptors on arcuate NPY/AgRP neurons
Inhibits NPY release, thereby lifting tonic inhibition on POMC neurons
Acts as an effective physiological brake on postprandial meal continuation

right.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 (GLP-1)
points: Co-secreted with PYY from intestinal L-cells upon luminal nutrient transit
Activates vagal sensory afferents and hypothalamic GLP-1 receptors
Slows gastric emptying and centrally suppresses hunger sensations
Potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells

steps.tx: Congenital genetic mutations affecting the melanocortin signaling pathway disrupt central energy homeostasis. In humans, heterozygous or homozygous loss-of-function mutations in the **melanocortin-4 receptor** represent the most common monogenic cause of severe early-onset obesity, producing insatiable post-weaning hyperphagia, accelerated linear growth, and hyperinsulinemia.
steps.say: Mutations in the melanocortin-4 receptor cause severe early-onset obesity due to uninhibited hunger.
